case.title: A lead change message names the work order and technician, with Undo
case.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Technicians {Technician-A} and {Technician-B} are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role and Time Clock on.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682424 Ana and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C682424 Ben.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has four Approved work orders: {Work-order-1} with no lead technician, and {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-3} and {Work-order-4} led by {Technician-A}. None has a shift booked on the Schedule.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682424 Toast Words, and {Work-order-1} to {Work-order-4} are S2-37421 to S2-37424.
  • No line of {Work-order-1} has a technician, and {Technician-B} is not the technician on any line of {Work-order-3}. {Work-order-4} has a line, {Line-1}, whose technician is {Technician-B}, set on the line itself.
    For example: {Line-1} is "Brake inspection".
  • The design picture DC-21-toast-light-1440.png is attached to this case.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Board View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
case.custom_steps:
1. Drag the card for {Work-order-1} from "Unassigned" onto {Technician-A}'s column and let go.
  2. Compare the message at the bottom right with the attached picture DC-21-toast-light-1440.png.
  3. Open the "More actions" (…) menu on the card for {Work-order-2}.
  4. Click "Unassign".
  5. Read the message at the bottom right.
  6. Click "Tech View" in the display switcher.
  7. Open the "More actions" (…) menu on the row for {Work-order-3}.
  8. Click "Reassign lead technician".
  9. Click {Technician-B} in the list.
  10. Read the message at the bottom right.
  11. Drag the row for {Work-order-4} from {Technician-A}'s group onto {Technician-B}'s group and let go.
  12. Read the message at the bottom right.
case.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Work-order-1} moves into {Technician-A}'s column.
  • Step 2: a white message box at the bottom right, with a round green check icon, reads "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-A}" and has an "Undo" button and a close (×) button, laid out as in the picture.
  • Step 3: the menu offers "Unassign".
  • Step 4: {Work-order-2} moves to "Unassigned".
  • Step 5: the message reads "{Work-order-2} moved to Unassigned" and has an "Undo" button.
  • Step 6: Tech View shows {Work-order-3} in {Technician-A}'s group.
  • Step 7: the menu offers "Reassign lead technician".
  • Step 8: the "Reassign lead technician" dialog opens.
  • Step 9: the dialog closes and {Work-order-3} moves to {Technician-B}'s group.
  • Step 10: the message reads "{Work-order-3} assigned to {Technician-B}" and has an "Undo" button.
  • Step 11: {Work-order-4} moves to {Technician-B}'s group.
  • Step 12: the message reads "{Work-order-4} lead technician set to {Technician-B}" and has an "Undo" button.

Known problem (SV-11524, open; seen on staging by the designer on 19 Oct 2026): the message reads "Lead technician updated" (or "Lead technician removed") and has no Undo button. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 19 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician from the board or grouped table); tickets SV-11522 (Tech View) and SV-11524 (Board View)

  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”
  • PRD change log, 19 Oct 2026: “S4-R5, S4-R16, new S4-R32: the lead-change toast is the design’s toast, “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}” / “{work order number} unassigned”, with Undo; 8 seconds, held while hovered; Undo restores the lead, the order position and any cleared shifts (was: standard toast “Lead technician updated” / “Lead technician removed”, no Undo; reverses the SV-11396 call for these two toasts). v66.”
  • PRD change log, 19 Oct 2026 (v68): “S4-R5: the toast follows the design: “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead (was “{work order number} unassigned”), and “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already on a line. v68.”

Not yet checked against a build.

References from Design

Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), file "Work Orders.dc.html", export of 14 Oct 2026, read 19 Oct 2026: the lead-change toast with Undo (the picture to compare against at step 2).

Design pictures attached to this case: DC-21-toast-light-1440.png.

Design and PRD: The picture's words come from the design's example data ("S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards"). Since PRD version 68 (19 Oct 2026) S4-R5 uses the design's wording, including "lead technician set to" and "moved to Unassigned"; compare the picture for the look, and check the words given in the expected results.

  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, the toast with Undo: “<div role="status" style="position: fixed; right: 24px; bottom: 24px; z-index: 300; width: 400px;”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, the toast's Undo button: “font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--sv-text-primary);" style-hover="background: var(--sv-surface-hover); border-color: var(--sv-border-strong);">Undo</button>”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, the toast's close button: “aria-label="Dismiss"”

AUTOMATION: READY - EXPECT FAIL (SV-11524)
